notes.claim: A quadratic's graph is a U-shaped curve called a parabola.
A rectangle with sides x+2 and x+3 has its area written two ways: as the product of two binomials, and as the sum of its four smaller rectangles' areas.
Expanding double brackets means multiplying every term in the first bracket by every term in the second.
The MCA Second Engineer mathematics syllabus calls a two-term bracket a binomial expression (2.1.11).
The MCA Second Engineer mathematics syllabus names ax² + bx + c, with x² its highest power, a quadratic (2.1.33).
To factorise x² + bx + c into two brackets, the two numbers must add to b and multiply to c.
If two numbers multiply to zero, at least one of them is zero: if ab = 0 then a = 0 and/or b = 0.
Completing the square rewrites a quadratic as a perfect square plus a constant.
In letters, completing the square turns ax² + bx + c into a(x + b/2a)² + (c − b²/4a).
Writing a quadratic in completed-square form gives the coordinates of its turning point.
The MCA Second Engineer mathematics syllabus asks for stating and using the general formula for a quadratic; none of its lines read for this course names completing the square.
SQA's HN unit Engineering Mathematics 1 (H7K0 33) has no outcome on quadratics; it says it would be advantageous if learners had good algebraic skills on entry.
The quadratic formula for ax² + bx + c = 0 is x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a.
Completing the square with letters turns ax² + bx + c into a(x + b/2a)² + (c − b²/4a).
The discriminant b² − 4ac distinguishes two distinct real roots, one repeated real root, or only non-real complex roots.
The SQA National 5 2023 course report gives the expected words for the nature of the roots: two real and distinct roots, one repeated real root or two equal real roots, no real roots.
OpenStax Physics solves a firework shell's time of flight from the quadratic 4.90t² − 14.3t − 20.0 = 0, with a = 4.90, b = −14.3 and c = −20.0, by the quadratic formula.
OpenStax gives its two solutions as t = 3.96 s and −1.03 s and discards the negative time as an event before the start of motion.
If a > 0 the parabola opens upward; if a < 0 it opens downward.
The y-intercept of any parabola y = ax² + bx + c is the point (0, c).
A parabola's graph is a U-shaped curve, and the quadratic's turning point can be read from its completed-square form.
The maximum height of a parabola sits in the middle of its two roots.
In metres and seconds a thrown object's height is h(t) = −4.9t² + v₀t + h₀, where −4.9 is half of gravity's roughly 9.8 m/s².
Standard gravity, 9.80665 m/s², is an arbitrarily defined value used to define force units, not the gravity at one particular place.
The thrown object's maximum height sits in the middle of the two times at which its height is zero.
A battery's output power vanishes at no load (I = 0) and at short circuit (I = ε/r), and peaks when the load resistance equals the internal resistance r.
At maximum power the current is ε/(2r), half the short-circuit current ε/r.
A simply supported beam's bending moment must be zero at its two supported ends.
For a simply supported beam with a uniformly distributed load w over span L, the maximum bending moment is wL²/8, and the peak lands at midspan.
For i7: a beam's bending moment at a section is the sum of the moments of all the forces on one side of that section.
For i7: a uniformly distributed load acts, for its turning effect, as one force at the centre of the loaded length.
A polynomial is an expression of the form a + bx + cx² + dx³ + and so on, a sum of powers of x.
The factor theorem says that if P(a) = 0, then x − a is a factor of P(x).
A polynomial equation of degree n has n roots; some may be repeated and some may be complex (Sheffield's copy of HELM 3.3), so a cubic meets the x-axis at most three times.
The remainder theorem: dividing f(x) by x − c leaves f(c), so the remainder needs no division.
Where cubics turn up: ship power is often roughly proportional to the cube of the speed (USNA).
